transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue Jul 29 2025
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~62 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Morgan (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Priya (CTO), James (Platform), Leah (InfoSec), Samir (SRE)

Summary section (auto):
- High level: Stratus wants a private deployment with strict egress control and residency in eu-west-1 + us-east-1. Deciding between VPC Peering and PrivateLink.
- Pilot goal: validate latency SLOs and deployment topology, run benchmarks for cost unit economics.

Transcript:
[00:00] Morgan: hey everyone, thanks for joining on short notice, i'm Morgan from Redwood. i'll kick off quick, then carlos will do the deep infra bits.
[00:12] Priya: hey Morgan, thanks. we want to be explicit, our main concerns are residency and egress — some requests can never leave eu-west-1, and we have POA for that.
[00:22] Morgan: totally — that's what we'll scope today. carlos, want to give a quick overview of the deployment options?
[00:28] Carlos: yeah, sure. so, two primary options for private connectivity to Redwood Private: VPC peering into our dedicated VPC vs AWS PrivateLink endpoints. Peering gives route-level access but requires cross-account route tables, whereas PrivateLink presents an interface endpoint and keeps traffic path more tightly controlled.
[00:45] James: uh quick Q — with PrivateLink does egress still touch public subnet for some things? we can't have nat gateway egress hitting the internet for token streams.
[00:54] Carlos: good question. PrivateLink keeps the session inside AWS backbone to the endpoint service. however, if you use cross-region fallback we might route across regions; you can opt to disable cross-region fallback to enforce region lock. small gotcha is service endpoints still resolve to regional infra; there's no NAT to internet unless you explicitly allow outbound.
[01:10] Leah: from compliance, we need KMS integration and a proof that logs are retained for 13 months. is that supported in the private model?
[01:18] Morgan: yes, we can integrate with customer KMS and ship audit logs to your CloudWatch/ S3 bucket with retention policies. we'll share the SOC2 artifact and our recommended KMS key policy.
[01:28] Samir: would you need cross-account IAM roles? how intrusive is the infra change?
[01:34] Carlos: minimal. for PrivateLink we ask you to create VPC endpoints and security groups, and provide the endpoint id to us. For peering, you accept a peering request and update route tables. neither requires sys-admin-level changes to your apps, but peering opens more network surface area.
[01:50] Priya: okay, we're leaning PrivateLink because Security doesn't like peering, but we need cost and perf tradeoffs.
[01:57] Morgan: noted. let's talk success criteria — what would you consider a successful pilot?
[02:02] Priya: success is twofold: 1) meet p95 latency below 200ms for chat-generated responses at our expected load, 2) deployment proves that no egress leaves eu-west-1 for designated tenant traffic. third, we want cost per 1k tokens baseline.
[02:18] Carlos: to clarify, is the 200ms p95 end-to-end or just inference service?
[02:22] Priya: end-to-end from our app to the response including network.
[02:26] Carlos: okay. typical inference-only p95 on similar setups is ~80-150ms for optimized LLMs under continuous batching, but network adds delta. we'll plan for an end-to-end bench that measures both.
[02:38] James: our traffic profile — avg request size 120 tokens, avg token gen 90 tokens, baseline ~120 req/s, spikes to 350 req/s for 10-15 minutes, concurrent users about 300. we can share exact traces after.
[02:53] Morgan: perfect — that gives us a sizing start. for the pilot we'll ask you to provision a staging account and we run a 24h soak + focused burst tests.
[03:03] Leah: for the benchmark, we need to see p99 for tail latency and cold-start numbers. we also want to verify that KV cache warm-up reduces cost over time.
[03:12] Carlos: we'll include p50/p95/p99, cold start (>30 min idle), sustained throughput test, and a cache-warmup run. we'll produce a benchmark script; tests will record token/sec, cost estimate, and occurance of fallbacks.
[03:22] Priya: fallback — you mean model fallback to smaller model if dedicated capacity is saturated?
[03:26] Carlos: right — our runtime can route to a compatible model variant if capacity constrained. for the pilot we'll keep routing fixed unless you want us to test graceful degrade.
[03:34] Morgan: also want to confirm region locking. you mentioned eu-west-1. do you want both eu-west-1-only and a secondary us-east-1 for DR?
[03:42] Priya: primary is eu-west-1-only. DR can be us-east-1 but must be opt-in and have explicit data residency rules. if failover happens we need a manual approve step for data movement.
[03:53] Samir: how do you prove residency? logs? network flow?
[03:56] Carlos: we'll provide request/response tracing with region metadata and we can route logs to your S3 bucket. we also can provide VPC flow logs to show traffic never left region.
[04:05] James: benchmarks — how long do you need to run? we prefer minimal downtime for staging.
[04:10] Morgan: standard is a 24h soak to capture diurnal patterns plus 3 focused burst windows (10, 15, 30 min) — total bench time ~6 hours of active load spread over 24h.
[04:20] Leah: for encryption, do you support bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via KMS? we need to ensure the keys never leave our control.
[04:26] Carlos: yes, BYOK supported. Redwood Private can be configured to use your AWS KMS CMK; we never hold plaintext keys. We'll send our KMS integration guide.
[04:35] Priya: about PrivateLink cost — is there additional per-GB cost on your side?
[04:39] Morgan: PrivateLink has AWS data processing charges; we'll include those in our cost estimates and show delta to peering. generally, peering has lower AWS egress but increases ops surface area.
[04:50] James: sounds reasonable. can we capture token-level cost during bench?
[04:54] Carlos: yes — our runtime produces token accounting per request and we can map that to cost model. we'll produce token/cost CSVs.
[05:02] Priya: timeline? we aim to have pilot running within two weeks. is that feasible?
[05:06] Morgan: feasible if you can provide staging account and endpoint by end of week. our typical lead for PrivateLink is 3-5 business days for config and then 24-48 hours to validate.
[05:16] Samir: security review — what artifacts do you need from us and what will you provide?
[05:20] Leah: we'll need proof of data deletion, key rotation policy, and access control matrix.
[05:24] Morgan: we'll provide SOC2 report, our attestation for egress controls, and sample key rotation docs. for access we'll use cross-account IAM roles with least privilege for bench only.
[05:33] James: one more — can we run a synthetic replay of our prod traces? that would be the most realistic.
[05:37] Carlos: absolutely. please scrub PII and send a sample trace, we can run it mirrored to reproduce patterns.
[05:43] Priya: okay let's recap actions.
[05:46] Morgan: recap: Redwood deliver network one-pager and bench script; customer to provide traffic profile and staging account; schedule bench kickoff; target pilot in two weeks.
[05:55] Leah: thanks — please send SOC2 redaction and KMS policy.
[05:58] Morgan: will do. any final Qs?
[06:01] Priya: no, thanks everyone.
[06:04] Morgan: thanks, we'll follow up with invites for the benchmark kickoff. bye.
